title: Security release exception rapid approval and audit spec
body:
Purpose:
This doc is a lightweight, prescriptive spec for handling release-time security exceptions and for validating the audit artifacts that must accompany any rapid approval. Put another way: when a release needs an exception to RBAC v2, audit export, or SIEM wiring to ship, this checklist + ticket template should get engineers and reviewers aligned quickly so the change is auditable and reversible.

Scope / when to use this:
- Emergency or near-release exceptions to RBAC v2 enforcement (temporary role grants, bypass flags)
- Known gaps in audit log schema or SIEM exports that would otherwise block release
- Short-term evidence automation failures (evidence pipeline degraded) with planned remediation
- Not for permanent policy changes; anything longer than 30 days must go through the full change review board (CRB) path.

Quick runbook (3–10 min triage):
1) Owner files a SEC-EXC- ticket using the template below (add "rapid-approval" label).
2) Pager/team lead posts the ticket link in #sec-release-approvals and @security-on-call.
3) Check the blocking dimension(s): RBAC / AuditExport / SIEM / EvidencePipeline. Mark in ticket.
4) If RBAC: validate minimum-scope grant (principle, duration, reason). If AuditExport: attach sample log lines to ticket. If SIEM: attach last 24h export sanity check.
5) Security reviewer approves with explicit TTL (max 72 hours) and lists mitigations. Approver must be security-on-call or delegated approver.
6) Engineering implements with feature flag + smoke tests; attach smoke results.
7) Auto-run evidence collector to snapshot logs and store in evidence bucket (see Evidence automation section).
8) After release, follow remediation plan (revoke grants / fix schema / restore pipeline) and update ticket.

RBAC v2 exception checklist (minimal gating items):
- Who is the principal? (OID / user/email): ___________
- Role being granted (exact role ID): ___________
- Required scope justification (two-line business justification): ___________
- TTL requested, and why TTL is safe: ___________
- Is this least-privilege (yes/no)? If no, why necessary? ___________
- Are there any dependent resources (datasets, KMS keys, private clusters)? List: ___________
- Mitigations while exception active (monitoring, extra logging, 2-person deploy): ___________
- Revoke plan owner and date: ___________
- Security reviewer (approve/reject + comments): ___________

Audit log schema validation checklist:
- Attach a sample of the generated audit logs showing the change; include timestamps and correlated request IDs.
- Confirm required fields present for downstream SIEM:
  Required audit fields (minimal):
    timestamp, request_id, principal_id, role_change, resource_type, resource_id, action, outcome, service, region, trace_parent
  Recommended enrichment fields:
    user_agent, client_ip, function_name, commit_sha, pipeline_run_id
- Sample audit CSV (paste into ticket):
  timestamp,request_id,principal_id,role_change,resource_type,resource_id,action,outcome,service,region,trace_parent,user_agent,commit_sha
  2025-01-15T18:21:02Z,req-23b4,alice@example.com,grant:rbac/infra-read,project,proj-7,assign,success,auth-service,us-west-2,00f1a2b3-...,curl/7.82.0,abc123
- Schema quirks to watch for: null vs empty-string for resource_id, nested JSON in role_change fields (avoid), timestamp timezone normalization.
- Validate log signing/hashing if required by policy.

SIEM export verification (fast checks):
- Confirm exports landed in SIEM ingest path within last 30 minutes for at least 5 representative entries.
- Verify a sample query in SIEM returns the attached request_id. Query example: "request_id: \"req-23b4\" AND service:auth-service"
- Check mapping: audit.timestamp -> siem._time, audit.principal_id -> user.id, audit.action -> event.action. Document any mismatched fields in the ticket.
- If export is delayed or missing fields, include delta (how many fields missing) and whether a backfill is needed.

Evidence automation snapshot (what we expect the pipeline to produce and how to provide a fallback):
- The evidence pipeline must produce a ZIP with:
  - audit-snapshot.json (newline-delimited json of audit events)
  - siem-sample.txt (SIEM query and response snippet)
  - rbacevidence.txt (RBAC delta: who granted what)
  - smoke-results.txt (tests that exercised the change)
- If automation unavailable, manual attach: compressed logs + explicit steps to reproduce the audit event. Label as "manual-evidence" and include duration of manual period.
- Evidence retention: put snapshot into s3://redwood-sec-evidence/releases/YYYY-MM-DD/TICKETID/ with read-only ACL for security reviewers.

Exception approval matrix (who can approve what):
- Security on-call: can approve RBAC exceptions up to 24h TTL for non-prod, 4h TTL for prod emergency.
- InfoSec manager: can approve RBAC up to 72h for prod; must escalate to CRB if >72h.
- Observability lead: can approve schema-forwarding or SIEM mapping exceptions for up to 7 days if compensating controls exist.
- Product/PM: must sign off on business risk for exceptions that touch customer data.

Ticket template (copy into new SEC-EXC- ticket body):
- Title: [rapid-approval] short summary (RBAC|AUDIT|SIEM|EVIDENCE) - Service - Region
- Affects: prod/staging/dev
- Blocking dimension: select one: RBAC / AuditExport / SIEM / EvidencePipeline / Other
- Owner: name + email + pager on-call
- Proposed change: concise description (commands, PR link)
- TTL requested (iso8601 end time)
- Minimal scope (principals, roles, resource ids)
- Attached evidence: (audit-sample, siem-sample, smoke-results)
- Mitigations while active:
- Revoke plan and tests to validate revoke:
- Security reviewer notes and explicit approval line (approver name, timestamp, TTL approved)

Approval wording (required in ticket):
"I, <name>, approve this exception for principal <principal> to carry out <change> until <iso8601 end>. Review required at <end - 24h>. Approver role: <security-on-call | infosec-manager | observability-lead>"

Post-release remediation (must be added to same ticket):
- Revoke grants within TTL window (include revoke command + who ran it)
- Submit follow-up PRs to fix root cause (schema change, pipeline fix) and link PRs.
- Evidence re-run: generate second snapshot showing revoke and updated schema.
- Close ticket only after evidence and PRs merged or CRB-approved timeline attached.

Audit considerations for long-term telemetry (notes / ideas):
- If we see repeated short TTL exceptions for the same role/resource, flag for a policy exception review and potential permanent role redesign.
- Consider adding a new audit field: exception_ticket = <ticket-id> to correlate ephemeral grants. This would simplify retrospective queries in SIEM.

Open questions / TODOs:
- Should we standardize the exact filename format for the evidence snapshot? (current proposal: evidence-<ticket>-<ts>.zip)
- Can the evidence pipeline auto-add the ticket id to audit records? (engineering + infra followup: GH PR linked above)
- Do we require signed log hashes for rapid approvals or only for CRB escalations?

Appendix A: quick checklist for approver (checkboxes to paste into ticket)
- [ ] Confirm principal identity and validate MFA status
- [ ] Confirm minimal-scope grant (no wider than required)
- [ ] TTL set and reasonable for the risk profile
- [ ] Evidence attached (audit-sample + SIEM snippet + smoke results)
- [ ] Revoke plan exists and owner assigned
- [ ] Notes recorded about compensating controls

Appendix B: handy commands / snippets (examples)
- Grant (example):
  redwood rbac grant --principal alice@example.com --role rbac/infra-read --resource project:proj-7 --ttl 4h --ticket SEC-EXC-1287
- Revoke (example):
  redwood rbac revoke --grant-id grant-9f2a --ticket SEC-EXC-1287
- Generate audit sample (dev):
  curl -H \"Authorization: Bearer $TOKEN\" https://auth.redwood.ai/v1/grants/last?limit=5 > audit-sample.json

If anything in this doc is unclear, drop a note in #sec-release-approvals or tag me (Asha) and I'll triage.

-- End of spec --
